calls.reason: Common Sense Media found serious risks to teens, but the FTC inquiry and CRS account do not establish whether federal safeguards were coherent or adequate. The evidence supports vulnerability without settling the whole claim.

New York’s official notice confirms that companion chatbots faced binding suicide and self-harm safeguards from November 5, before Marcus’s statement. That directly undercuts the claim that these bots lacked regulation.

Congress passed the targeted TAKE IT DOWN Act, while CRS reported no broad AI regulatory legislation. In context, Marcus’s evaluative wording could mean standards sufficient to replace state protections; these records do not settle that.
